explanation: Cuba is bigger than Hispaniola, Jamaica and Puerto Rico put together. When Christopher Columbus reached its coast, he believed it was part of mainland Asia.

claims.text: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.
Hispaniola, Jamaica and Puerto Rico are each smaller than Cuba.
Cuba is larger than Hispaniola, Jamaica and Puerto Rico combined.
When Christopher Columbus reached Cuba, he believed it was part of the Asian mainland.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check run for the batch and writer; no errors or warnings on this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed, distractors included; c1 (superlative) and c3 (number) are high under the C26 floor, and c2 and c4 are standard. Datasets: mledoze-countries areas: CUB 109,884; HTI 27,750 and DOM 48,671, the two countries of Hispaniola, together 76,421; JAM 10,991; PRI 8,870 (c1, c2). The last three islands together come to 96,282, less than Cuba (c3). These are country totals that include small offshore islands on both sides; the main islands compare the same way, because Cuba's main island alone is far larger than Hispaniola. Rival test: Hispaniola is the strong rival, a big island shared by two countries, then Jamaica and Puerto Rico. Against the key: nothing; Cuba leads by a wide margin. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: The Caribbean's islands are known worldwide; no local knowledge is needed. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight apostrophes, explanation of 25 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. External evidence: none beyond the dataset; c4 is standard history. Seed: 2 (easy): most players pick Cuba; a few go for Hispaniola. Counterintuitive: false. Doubts: none.

evidence.excerpt: CUB "area": 109884; DOM "area": 48671; HTI "area": 27750; BHS "area": 13943; JAM "area": 10991; PRI "area": 8870

claimResults.note: Country areas: Cuba's 109,884 km² is the largest in the Caribbean subregion. Hispaniola is shared by DOM and HTI, so it is at most 76,421 km². Cuba's offshore islands (Isla de la Juventud the largest) are small, so the main island alone still far exceeds Hispaniola, and every other Caribbean island sits in a smaller country or territory.

Cuba's country area beats the sum of the other three by 14%. Compared island to island the margin narrows but holds (the main island of Cuba is usually given as about 104,500 km², knowledge), so the claim stands.

evidence.restatement: Columbus believed Cuba was part of the Asian mainland, and on his second voyage in 1494 he had his crew swear it was a continent.
